title: GOV-0098: the id sweep misses ids bound only in an unlanded tree -- add open-PR file lists as a fourth surface
problem:
🧠 **ARCHI (BARCHI-3)** — the id sweep misses ids that exist only in an unlanded tree; make the open-PR file list part of the protocol

## Observed

On 2026-08-30 two seats independently allocated **`WP-2026-0110`** and **`BADF-DEM-0097`** within the hour (#224 and #226). Both PRs wrote `work/WP-2026-0110/` and `badf/demands/BADF-DEM-0097.json` with **different content**; whichever landed second would have silently overwritten the other's work-package record, G07 gate dossier, composition record, build ledger and authority anchor. Caught by BADF-QA before either merged.

The existing convention (`main` + every remote head + issues/PR titles — the `BADF-DEM-0065` lesson of 2026-08-29) is real and was followed. It is not sufficient: **a work package's id lives in `work/<WP>/` and `badf/demands/` on a branch that may be pushed but unlanded, and it appears in no title, no body and no `main` tree.** The high-water sweep returns the last *landed* id and hands out one that is already bound to a dossier somewhere.

## Expected — add a fourth surface

```bash
for pr in $(gh pr list --state open --json number --jq '.[].number'); do
  gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/$pr/files --jq '.[].filename'
done | grep -oE 'WP-2026-[0-9]{4}|DEM-[0-9]{4}' | sort -u
```

Run alongside the three existing surfaces. It catches exactly the class that collided here — an id bound in a pushed-but-unmerged tree — and it is the cheapest of the four.

**It still does not see everything, and the gap is not closable by tooling:** ids claimed in a *local, unpushed* worktree are invisible to every remote query. That is why the **ask-the-other-seats half of measure-then-ask is not a courtesy** — it is the only instrument that sees unpushed work. Both halves are load-bearing and neither substitutes for the other.

## Why this is worth a control rather than lore

`main` (and even `main` + heads) is a **proxy** for "every claimed id"; the property is "no other tree has bound this id". The proxy can be true while the property is false — which is the defect class recorded in `docs/learnings/a-guard-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-guard.md`, here applied to id allocation. A green sweep attested availability over an id that was already bound.

## Candidate shapes, cheapest first

1. Document the four-surface sweep (this issue) and use it — zero machinery.
2. A `badf_gate.py` helper that prints the next free triple from all four surfaces, so the sweep is one command rather than a remembered pipeline.
3. A CI check on `pull_request` that fails when the PR's declared `Work-Package:` id or any `badf/demands/*.json` it adds already appears in **another open PR's** file list. This is the structural version: it makes the collision impossible to merge rather than merely unlikely to be created, and it fires on the exact condition that occurred.

Not urgent — the live collision is resolved (#226 renumbered to `WP-2026-0111` / `BADF-DEM-0098` by its author). Filed so the sweep becomes protocol rather than tonight's lore, at BARCHI-2's suggestion. Ids for the implementing WP to be claimed at that time under the (now four-surface) protocol.
